samples.question: This image shows one die face: a large rounded square with round pips on it. Four short grey ticks are drawn inward from the middle of each of the four edges of the square; they are fixed decoration and are drawn the same way in every image of this set. The centre point of the face is where the line joining the top and bottom ticks crosses the line joining the left and right ticks. Round pips of the same colour may also appear on the background outside the square; those never count. Judge only what is drawn inside the square, and do not use how many pips a real die shows or where a real die puts them. The centre point counts as covered when it lies inside one of the pips on the face, and uncovered when it lies on bare face colour. Is the centre point of the face covered by a pip? Answer yes or no.
